_comment: Stanford MyHealth template. To complete: log into MyHealth.Stanford.edu, open DevTools, follow the discovery procedure in tools/v3/README.md, replace each TODO with the captured value. Per C-017 this is the path to recover Stanford's ~165 unscraped clinical notes (the IsClinicalNoteAvailable=True visits from stanford_visits_raw.json).
name: Stanford MyHealth

auth._comment: The anti-forgery-token pattern is universal across Epic-based portals. If Stanford uses a different selector or header (unlikely), update here. Verify by inspecting any XHR request from MyHealth in DevTools Network tab.

visits._comment: Stanford's visits list lives in an Epic SPA component. UCSF uses instance 7; Stanford's number may differ. To find it: in DevTools console run `Epic.PatientAccess.Components.__Instances.map((x,i)=>({i,t:x?.constructor?.name,n:x?.RenderedData?.length}))` and look for the one whose RenderedData length matches the visit count visible in the UI.

discovery.instance: TODO: discover via console probe described above

endpoint._comment: Stanford's visit-detail endpoint path may differ from UCSF's. To find: click a visit in the UI; in DevTools Network tab note the POST that returns the visit details JSON; copy its path here, and inspect the body to confirm the fields below match.
endpoint.path: TODO: e.g. /api/visits/past-details/GetVisitDetailsPast — verify in Network tab

notes._comment: Stanford's note-content endpoint analogous to UCSF's LoadReportContent. Same discovery procedure as for visits above: click a visit with a note, expand the note, capture the POST.
notes.filter: TODO: the path in the visit-details response where notesInfo lives may differ from UCSF; inspect a Stanford visit-details response to confirm the path under item.response

endpoint.path: TODO: e.g. /api/report-content/LoadReportContent — verify in Network tab

body_template._comment: Stanford may not require all UCSF fields, and may require additional ones. Map by inspecting a real request body.
